question: In which of the following groups of States and Union Territories is 'slash and burn' agriculture known as 'Dipa'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh and Andaman & Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Slash and burn' agriculture is known as 'Dipa' in the tribal regions of **Chhattisgarh and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.**
 
• 'Dipa' is a traditional form of agriculture practiced by indigenous communities where forests are cleared and burned for farming.
 
• This method is primarily used for cultivating crops like rice, millets, and vegetables in these regions.
 
• The practice is prevalent among tribal communities due to its simplicity and adaptation to local environmental conditions.
 
• While it serves as a subsistence farming method, it has ecological implications such as deforestation and soil degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slash and Burn Agriculture:**

 
 
• Also known as shifting cultivation, it involves clearing vegetation and burning it to enrich the soil with nutrients.
 
• Commonly practiced in tropical regions around the world.
 
• The method is often unsustainable due to soil erosion and biodiversity loss.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Impact:**
 
 
• Deforestation leads to loss of wildlife habitats and carbon sequestration capacity.
 
• Burning vegetation releases greenhouse gases, contributing to climate change.
 
• Soil fertility declines after repeated cycles, leading to abandonment of the land.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Sustainable Practices:**
 
 
• Agroforestry integrates crops and trees to maintain soil fertility.
 
• Crop rotation helps preserve soil nutrients and reduce pest risks.
 
• Terrace farming prevents soil erosion in hilly areas.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Slash and burn agriculture is practiced under different names worldwide, such as 'Milpa' in Central America and 'Kaingin' in the Philippines.
 
• Efforts are being made internationally to replace it with more sustainable farming methods.
